name: Schoenoplectus

project_scope.installer_dependency: S. californicus not canonical; installer owns species.

look_here_first: At the junction where the flowering branches leave the apparent stem, identify the erect continuation bract. Then cut a mid-height culm and compare its section. Finally dissect a fully ripe spikelet: count and examine the bristles around a single achene with a 10× lens. A triangular stem alone is not a species diagnosis.
shared_genus_traits: Rhizomatous colonial emergent sedges with basal sheaths and often reduced leaf blades.
Many tiny flowers under individual scales, gathered in spikelets; each mature flower produces a single achene.
The erect lowermost inflorescence bract looks like a continuation of the culm, making the branched head appear lateral.

species_comparison_matrix.caution: Height varies with water depth and growing conditions.

species_comparison_matrix.californicus: Compare perianth and achene outline; exact measurements pending
species_comparison_matrix.caution: One-seeded achene, not a multi-seeded capsule; immature fruit misleads.
Overlaps strongly; use with reproductive anatomy.

overlap_cautions: Do not use the triangular-versus-round culm shortcut alone: californicus can be bluntly angled and nearly round toward its base.
Sheath fronts overlap; check multiple stems and mature reproductive structures.
Use a ripe achene plus attached perianth, not loose fragments or a blurry whole-head photograph.
S. californicus is a source-pool comparison only until the installer confirms a canonical species; no range status is inferred.

comparison_cards.title: Round softstem versus bluntly angled bulrush
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Cut both culms at the same middle height; compare angle and spongy interior.
comparison_cards.caution: Stem geometry changes along the culm; not decisive alone.

comparison_cards.title: Bristles versus fringed perianth
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Dissect multiple ripe achenes and count the surrounding structures under 10–20×.
comparison_cards.caution: Usually six backward-barbed slender bristles in tabernaemontani versus typically 2–4 broader fringed members in californicus; check actual material.

comparison_cards.title: Bulrush versus cattail or other sedges
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Find the individual spikelets and the continuation bract.
comparison_cards.caution: Typha has dense cylindrical spike zones; Eleocharis often has a single terminal spikelet; Cyperus has different conspicuous bracts and inflorescence architecture.

genus_diagnostics.look_here_first: Continuation bract → mid-culm section → ripe spikelet scale → achene with perianth.
